thread:
Maria G.: Heads up — vuln flagged in transitive lib 'jwt-utils' (CVE-2026-2244). Affects our control-plane token parsing. Severity: HIGH. Possible token forgery in edge cases. Need quick triage on customer exposure and patch window.

Ajay K.: Oncall triage — any evidence of auth bypass in prod logs?

Sophia L.: Quick grep so far: no 401->200 spikes. Library is pulled into kube webhook and the auth middleware. Looks plausibly exploitable with crafted token values. Recommend patch asap, but we should mitigate first.

Maria G.: @Ajay if we patch control-plane containers we'll cause rolling restarts — estimate ~30s per pod, ~0.5-1% requests dropped during each pod restart. Hosted customers: low SLA impact. Dedicated customers: likely want advance notice.

Ajay K.: Proposal: 1) immediate WAF rule to block suspicious token patterns (1h), 2) canary patch in staging (3h), 3) phased rollout to hosted small shard (6-12h), 4) contact Dedicated customers for opt-in overnight window. @ops-oncall ok?

ops-oncall: WAF rule yes, we can push a quick header check in the edge proxy. Ops can own staged rollout and monitor. Night window available 02:00-04:00 UTC if needed.

Sophia L.: Mitigation idea — add strict token format validation at proxy level: drop malformed tokens. nginx snippet: ``if ($http_authorization !~ "^Bearer [A-Za-z0-9\._-]+$") { return 400; }`` That buys us time without rotating keys.

Maria G.: Important: do NOT rotate KMS keys unless we have confirmed exploit; key rotation will force client re-auth in some Dedicated setups and is heavy.

Ajay K.: Agreed. Only rotate if evidence. Also: add audit log entry for any deploys and decisions. We'll record deploy id + mitigation steps.

Sophia L.: I'll prepare the patch PR and the short test plan. Patch will be `pip install 'jwt-utils==1.2.5'` and we will run `kubectl rollout restart deployment control-plane --namespace=infra` for staged rollout.

sec-bot: Auto: new SNYK alert CVE-2026-2244 assigned to eng-security. Link: https://snyk.io/vuln/CVE-2026-2244

Maria G.: Who owns customer comms? Need a short notice: 'We're rolling a security patch to address a vulnerability in a transitive dependency. No evidence of customer impact. Minimal downtime expected during rolling updates.' Will post draft to #customer-success. @Sophia L. can you draft?

Sophia L.: Yep will draft and post. Suggest including expected downtime per pod and the scheduled windows, and offering Dedicated customers an opt-in for managed patch in the 02:00-04:00 UTC window.

Ajay K.: Assigning owners: @Sophia L. — patch + comms; @Ajay K. — rollout; @Maria G. — coordinate SRE canary and exec notifications. I'll be oncall during rollout.

Maria G.: Also add an RBAC note: canary will ship an optional stricter auth validation flag disabled by default for Dedicated until they opt-in. Add that to the runbook PR.

ops-oncall: We'll monitor latency/error budgets and keep rollback steps ready: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/control-plane --namespace=infra`.

Maria G.: If we get any indicators of exploitation we escalate to P0 and enact token revocation plan. For now proceed with the phased approach and mitigation rules. Posting status updates here. :thumbsup:
